body_markdown:
**More than 51,000 toothpaste and mouthwash products have been recalled across the United States after testing detected potentially harmful hormone contamination. The recall affects six ORL Organic Oral Care products, including two varieties marketed specifically for children. Consumers are being urged to stop using the affected products immediately.**


A nationwide recall has been issued for more than 51,000 units of toothpaste and mouthwash following concerns that the products may contain unexpected hormone ingredients.


The recall was initiated by ORL Labs LLC, an Arizona-based company operating under the ORL Organic Oral Care brand, after testing conducted by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) identified the presence of certain hormones in product samples.


The substances detected included progesterone, estradiol and dehydroepiandrosterone, commonly known as DHEA. These substances are associated with various hormonal functions in the human body and are not approved ingredients for ordinary toothpaste or mouthwash.


The affected products were distributed nationwide, raising concerns among consumers who may have purchased them for everyday oral hygiene.


## Which Toothpaste and Mouthwash Products Have Been Recalled?


The recall covers six products sold under the ORL Organic Oral Care brand. These include three toothpaste varieties packaged in four-ounce tubes and three mouthwash varieties sold in 16.9-ounce bottles.


The affected flavours include Fresh Mint, Cinnamint and Bubblegum Kids.


The recalled products are:


**Toothpaste products:**


- ORL Organic Oral Care Fresh Mint Natural Toothpaste, 4 oz.
- ORL Organic Oral Care Cinnamint Toothpaste, 4 oz.
- ORL Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids Natural Toothpaste, 4 oz.


**Mouthwash products:**


- ORL Organic Oral Care Fresh Mint Mouthwash, 16.9 oz.
- ORL Organic Oral Care Cinnamint Kids Mouthwash, 16.9 oz.
- ORL Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids Mouthwash, 16.9 oz.


Two products, the Bubblegum Kids toothpaste and Bubblegum Kids mouthwash, were specifically marketed for children.


The affected products were sold with expiration dates extending from September 2026 through August 2028, according to the recall records.


Consumers should check the product packaging, lot numbers and UPC codes carefully rather than assuming that every product from the brand is affected.


## Why Have the Products Been Recalled?


According to the FDA, laboratory testing identified the presence of progesterone, estradiol or DHEA in samples of the affected products.


The agency attributed the problem to potential cross-contamination.


Cross-contamination can occur when unwanted substances accidentally enter products during manufacturing, processing or packaging. One possible explanation is shared manufacturing equipment or facilities used to produce different types of products. However, the exact cause of this particular incident has not been publicly established.


The FDA reported that the company was notified of the testing results and subsequently initiated a voluntary recall.


The recall began on October 12, 2026, and was classified as Class II by the FDA on November 6.


## What Are Progesterone, Estradiol and DHEA?


The three substances identified during testing are hormones that play important roles in the human body.


**Progesterone** is a naturally occurring hormone involved in the menstrual cycle and pregnancy. It is also used in certain prescription treatments, including hormone therapy and some contraceptive methods.


**Estradiol** is a form of estrogen, a hormone that contributes to reproductive health, bone health and other bodily functions. Prescription estradiol is commonly used in hormone replacement therapy, particularly for people experiencing menopause-related symptoms.


**Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)** is a hormone produced naturally by the adrenal glands. The body uses it as a building block to produce other hormones, including testosterone and estrogen. DHEA is also available in some countries as a dietary supplement.


Although these substances have legitimate medical and biological functions, their presence in everyday oral care products raises concerns because toothpaste and mouthwash are not intended to deliver hormone treatments.


## What Health Risks Could Contaminated Toothpaste and Mouthwash Pose?


The potential health effects of exposure to the substances depend on several factors, including the amount present, frequency of exposure, individual health circumstances and whether the products were swallowed.


Possible side effects associated with hormone exposure can include headaches, drowsiness and breast tenderness.


However, the FDA has not established the precise concentration of the hormones detected in the affected toothpaste and mouthwash products.


It is therefore not possible to determine the level of exposure or predict the health effects for individual consumers based solely on the available recall information.


There are also unanswered questions about the potential effects on children, particularly those who may have used the Bubblegum Kids products.


Parents and caregivers should take particular care to check bathroom cabinets and household supplies for the recalled products.


Importantly, no illnesses or complications linked to the recalled products had been reported in the available recall coverage at the time of publication.


## FDA Classifies the Recall as Class II


The FDA has assigned the recall a Class II classification.


According to the agency, this category applies when exposure to or use of a recalled product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences, or when the likelihood of serious adverse health consequences is considered remote.


This classification does not mean that every person who used the products will experience health problems. However, it does indicate that the contamination is significant enough to warrant precautionary action.


Consumers should not continue using the products while waiting for further information.


## What Should Consumers Do If They Have Purchased the Products?


Anyone who has purchased one of the affected ORL Organic Oral Care products should take the following precautions:


1. **Stop using the products immediately.** Do not continue brushing with the recalled toothpaste or rinsing with the affected mouthwash.
2. **Check the packaging.** Compare the product name, flavour, size, UPC and lot number with the information published in the FDA recall records.
3. **Dispose of affected products.** Follow the company's recall instructions and avoid giving the products to other people.
4. **Contact the seller.** Consumers have been advised to contact the retailer or seller to request a full refund.
5. **Seek medical advice if concerned.** Anyone experiencing unusual symptoms after using the products should contact a healthcare professional. Parents should also seek professional advice if they are concerned about a child's exposure.


A complete list of affected lot numbers is available through the FDA's Enforcement Reports database.


## Why This Recall Matters for Everyday Oral Hygiene


Toothpaste and mouthwash are products that millions of people use regularly, often without giving much thought to their ingredients or manufacturing processes.


This recall highlights the importance of product safety testing and effective manufacturing controls, particularly for products marketed as natural or suitable for children.


The affected toothpastes were described as natural products and did not contain fluoride. However, natural labelling does not automatically guarantee that a product is free from contamination or other safety concerns.


Fluoride is an important ingredient in many conventional toothpastes because it helps strengthen tooth enamel and reduce the risk of cavities. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recognises community water fluoridation as an effective public health measure for preventing tooth decay.


Consumers should continue following established oral hygiene recommendations and choose suitable alternatives from reputable manufacturers.


The incident also serves as a reminder to pay attention to product recalls, particularly when items are used daily by children and other vulnerable household members.


## Final Thoughts


The recall of more than 51,000 ORL Organic Oral Care toothpaste and mouthwash products is an important consumer safety alert.


Although no related illnesses had been reported in the available coverage, the detection of progesterone, estradiol and DHEA in product samples has prompted the FDA to classify the incident as a Class II recall.


Consumers should check their products, stop using any affected items and contact the seller about obtaining a refund.


Until further information becomes available, avoiding the recalled products is the safest precaution.


**Source:** US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Enforcement Reports, ORL Labs LLC recall records, October 12 and November 6, 2026. Additional background: CDC information on fluoride and dental health.


**Disclaimer:** This article is intended for general information and consumer awareness purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis or treatment recommendations. The potential health effects of exposure may vary depending on individual circumstances and the level of exposure. Anyone concerned about possible exposure or experiencing symptoms should consult a qualified healthcare professional. Consumers should refer to the FDA's official recall information for the latest product details and instructions.
